## DEB growth

The DEB equations are based on @FLORESVALIENTE2023103034

Influene of temperature is given by equation 5 of @FLORESVALIENTE2023103034:

$$
c_T = \exp \left( \dfrac{T_A}{T_1} - \dfrac{T_A}{T} \right)
\left[
\dfrac{
1 +
\exp
\left(
\dfrac{T_{AL}}{T_1}
-
\dfrac{T_{AL}}{T_L}
\right)
+
\exp
\left(
\dfrac{T_{AH}}{T_H}
-
\dfrac{T_{AH}}{T_1}
\right)
}
{
1 +
\exp
\left(
\dfrac{T_{AL}}{T}
-
\dfrac{T_{AL}}{T_L}
\right)
+
\exp
\left(
\dfrac{T_{AH}}{T_H}
-
\dfrac{T_{AH}}{T}
\right)
}
\right]
$$ {#eq-deb-temp}

If the particle is not feeding ($E_H < E_{Hb}$), then the particle does not feed. Else, the functional response is computed as:

$$
f = \dfrac{F}{F + K}
$$ {#eq-deb-repfonct}

with $F$ the food vector and $K$ the half-saturation constant.

Assimilation rates $\{ \dot{p_{Am}} \}$, energy conductance $\dot{\gamma} = \dfrac{\{ \dot{p_{Am}}\}}{[E_m]} $, volume specific somatic maintenance ($[\dot{p_M} ]$) and maturity maintenances rates ($k_J$) are corrected by the $c_T$ factor.

If the accelerated DEB model is used, thr metabolic rate acceleration is computed as follows

$$
s_M =
\begin{cases}
 1 & (E < E_{HB})\\
 \dfrac{V^{1/3}}{L_b} & (E_{HB} \le E_H < E_{Hj}) \\
 \dfrac{L_j}{L_b} & (E_{H} > E_{Hj})
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-deb-sm}

with $L_b$ the length of the particle when $E_H > E_Hb$ (i.e the length at birth) and $L_j$ the length of the particlet when $E_H > E_Hj$ (i.e the length when metamorphosis occurs). The $s_M$ factor is then used to multiply the assimilation rate and the energy conductance.

Consequently, the assimilation (in $J.day^{-1}$) is computed as follows:

$$
\dot{p_A} = \begin{cases}
0 & (E_{H} < E_{Hb}) \\
\{ \dot{p_{Am}}\} \times s_M \times c_T \times f \times {V}^{2/3}  & (E_{H} \ge E_{Hb}) \\
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-deb-pA}


Energy loss to maintenance is given by

$$
\dot{p_M} = [ \dot{p_M} ] \times c_T \times V
$$ {#eq-deb-pM}

The mobilized energy is given by:

$$
\dot{p_C} =
\dfrac{\dfrac{E}{V} \times \left([E_G] \times \dot{\gamma} \times V^{2/3} + \dot{p_M}\right)}
{\kappa \dfrac{E}{V} + [E_G]}
$$ {#eq-deb-pC}

Maturity maintenance is given by

$$
\dot{p_J} = k_J \times c_T \times E_H
$$ {#eq-deb-pJ}

Energy that is sent to structural growth is given by:

$$
\dot{p_G} = \kappa \dot{p_C} - \dot{p_M}
$$ {#eq-deb-pG}

Energy that goes to reproduction is given by:

$$
\dot{p_R} = (1 - \kappa) \dot{p_C} - \dot{p_J}
$$ {#eq-deb-pR}

Finally, the increment of reserve $E$ and structural volume $V$ is given by:

$$
\dfrac{dE}{dt} = \dot{p_A} - \dot{p_C}
$$ {#eq-deb-dEdt}

$$
\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{\dot{p_G}}{{[E_G]}}
$$  {#eq-deb-dVdt}

The increment of the energy invested into development and reproduction depends on the value of $E_H$. If $$:

$$
\dfrac{dH}{dt} =
\begin{cases}
\dot{p_R} & E_H < E_{Hp}\\
0 &  E_H \ge E_{Hp}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-deb-dHdt}

$$
\dfrac{dR}{dt} =
\begin{cases}
0 & E_H < E_{Hp}\\
\dot{p_R} &  E_H \ge E_{Hp}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-deb-dRdt}


Finally, starvation mortality is determined whether one of the following conditions are matched:

$$
M_{starv} =
\begin{cases}
\kappa \dot{p_C} & < & \dot{p_M}\\
(1 - \kappa) {\dot{p_C}} < p_J
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-deb-starv}

Finally, all the states variables are then incremented:

$$
E(t + \Delta t) = E(t) + \dfrac{dE}{dt}\Delta t
$$ {#eq-deb-incr-e}

$$
V(t + \Delta t) = V(t) + \dfrac{dV}{dt}\Delta t
$$ {#eq-deb-incr-v}

$$
E_H(t + \Delta t) = E_H(t) + \dfrac{dE_H}{dt}\Delta t
$$ {#eq-deb-incr-h}

$$
E_R(t + \Delta t) = E_R(t) + \dfrac{dE_R}{dt}\Delta t
$$ {#eq-deb-incr-r}
